B1.rule: valid earlier/later pair (same AOI, later after earlier, maps exist)

B2.rule: same real-world event_id; calendar proximity is not sufficient

B3.rule: jointly valid transition mask (unknown never inferred)

B4.rule: no target leakage; in-horizon rain is POST-T0 OBSERVATION

B6.rule: transition signal: ≥20 pairs with new-flood or recession, mean turnover ≥0.01, ≥5 events; pixel count alone is not enough

B7.rule: ≥8 independent events represented by pairs (not pair count)

decision: TARGET B IS FEASIBLE BUT FORCING IS INSUFFICIENT
promising_narrative: Target B is an honest change label: mean jointly-valid IoU(t0,t1)=0.256, mean turnover=0.058, 131 eligible pairs show new inundation. That is more interpretable than occurrence@192 h, which Phase 6.7 showed is dominated by persistence/climatology. It is **not** automatically a better *forecast*: in-horizon rain is POST-T0 OBSERVATION (forecast-available NWP in the cube: False; observational completeness 0.956). Letter E is withheld: 6–72 h spatial maps remain unsupported, official event n is 15, and replacing Track A as a product target requires forecast-kind forcing, not a prettier diagnostic.
next_step: Keep Target B as the observational change diagnostic. Do not train yet. Next authorized step, if any: add FORECAST-kind (NWP) rain for `(t0, t1]` as an explicit forcing layer, or a no-training study of whether pre-t0 rain + state at t0 can rank new-flood pixels. Do not invent 24 h GFM maps. Do not enable `/api/v1/forecast/ai-spatial`.
